messages.content: Write an internal proposal asking leadership for a quarter of engineering time to pay down technical debt. Around 250 words.

output:
Placeholders in brackets — swap in your real numbers before sending.

---

**Proposal: One quarter of engineering time for debt paydown**
To: [Leadership] · From: [Name] · [Date]

**The ask:** Dedicate Q[N] to paying down technical debt. No new customer-facing features from the [platform] team for twelve weeks.

**Why now.** Our lead time on a small change has gone from three days to eleven over the past year. Two-thirds of that is spent waiting on a test suite that takes [47] minutes and fails randomly about [one run in five]. Engineers re-run it, get coffee, lose the thread. We are paying for that every day, in a currency nobody puts on a roadmap.

The other cost is on-call. [Six] of our last [ten] Sev-2 incidents traced back to the same two services — the ones everybody agrees should have been split up in [2023].

**What we'd do.** Three things, in order: cut the test suite to under ten minutes, split [service A] along its obvious seam, and retire the [legacy config loader] that four teams currently work around. Each has an owner and a written plan. Nothing speculative, nothing architectural for its own sake.

**What we'd measure.** Median PR-to-production time, test flake rate, and Sev-2 count, all baselined this month and reported weekly. If lead time hasn't improved by week eight, we stop and give the remaining time back.

**What it costs.** [Two] roadmap items slip a quarter: [X] and [Y]. I think that's the cheaper trade. The alternative is paying the same tax next year, plus interest.

Happy to walk through the plan in detail.
